key_insight: Represent video frames as single "delta tokens" in a vision foundation model feature space so a compact generative model can predict diverse future states with far fewer tokens and parameters.
problem_solved: Current generative world models are computationally expensive and discriminative models collapse to deterministic averages; this paper addresses the need for efficient, diverse video/world prediction with much lower token and model cost.
method: Encode frames into a pre-trained vision foundation model (VFM) feature space instead of pixel latents.
Compress temporal changes into lightweight "delta tokens"—one token per frame representing the feature-space change from the previous frame.
Train a compact generative model (e.g., transformer/autoregressive sampler) to predict sequences of delta tokens, then reconstruct future features/frames or feed them to downstream tasks.
impact: Enables fast, parameter-efficient generative world models that produce diverse future trajectories—useful for scaling video prediction, planning, and model-based RL in compute-constrained settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → VFM features → delta-token encoder → compact generative model → feature decoder / predicted frames
Timeline comparison: one-token-per-frame (delta tokens) vs many-token dense representations showing token-count reduction
Bar chart: model size / inference latency / FLOPs comparison (baseline generative model vs delta-token model)
Grid of example predicted futures illustrating diversity (multiple plausible continuations from same context)
paper_title: A Frame is Worth One Token: Efficient Generative World Modeling with Delta Tokens
paper_authors: Tommie Kerssies, Gabriele Berton, Ju He, Qihang Yu, Wufei Ma
